
/-!
# The canonical preimage of a Poisson boundary

On a Poisson boundary the canonical Möbius preimage is the boundary function itself: the pullback
of `Z f` along the logarithm is the Poisson sum of `f`, and the corpus's Möbius inversion of the
Poisson sum says exactly that the Möbius-weighted dilation sum recovers `f`.

The collar exchange acts on a Poisson boundary by the Fourier transform of the boundary: the
Poisson operator intertwines Fourier with multiplicative inversion, and `J` *is* multiplicative
inversion in the logarithmic coordinate.

* `deningerMobiusPreimage_poissonSource` : **`f_{Zf} = f` on the ray.**
* `deningerCollarExchange_poissonSource` : **`J(Zf) = Z(ℱf)`.**
-/

namespace RHTower

open SchwartzMap ArithmeticFunction GaloisForLFunctions

noncomputable section

/-- The pullback of a Poisson boundary is the Poisson sum. -/
theorem deningerLogPull_poissonSource (h : DeningerMeyerCap) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    deningerLogPull ((deningerPoissonSource h : DeningerExpSchwartz) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) x
      = deningerPoissonValue ((h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) x := by
  rw [deningerLogPull_apply, deningerPoissonSource_apply, deningerPoissonLog_eq,
    Real.exp_log hx]

/-- **The canonical Möbius preimage of a Poisson boundary is the boundary itself.** -/
theorem deningerMobiusPreimage_poissonSource (h : DeningerMeyerCap) {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) :
    deningerMobiusPreimage ((deningerPoissonSource h : DeningerExpSchwartz) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) x
      = ((h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) x := by
  have hinv := deningerMoebius_poissonValue ((h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ))
    (deningerMeyerCap_zero h.2) hx
  rw [deningerMoebiusValue] at hinv
  rw [deningerMobiusPreimage, ← hinv]
  refine tsum_congr fun n => ?_
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos n with rfl | hn
  · simp
  · have hnx : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) * x := by
      have hnr : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
      exact mul_pos hnr hx
    rw [deningerLogPull_poissonSource h hnx]

/-- Meyer's space is stable under the Fourier transform. -/
def deningerMeyerCapFourier (h : DeningerMeyerCap) : DeningerMeyerCap :=
  ⟨fourierSCLM ((h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)), deningerMeyerCap_fourierSCLM h.2⟩

@[simp]
theorem deningerMeyerCapFourier_coe (h : DeningerMeyerCap) :
    ((deningerMeyerCapFourier h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ))
      = fourierSCLM ((h : DeningerMeyerCap) : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) := rfl

/-- **The collar exchange of a Poisson boundary is the Poisson boundary of the Fourier
transform.**  The Poisson operator carries the Fourier involution to multiplicative inversion, and
in the logarithmic coordinate multiplicative inversion is exactly `J`. -/
theorem deningerCollarExchange_poissonSource (h : DeningerMeyerCap) :
    deningerCollarExchange (deningerPoissonSource h)
      = deningerPoissonSource (deningerMeyerCapFourier h) := by
  refine Subtype.ext (SchwartzMap.ext fun t => ?_)
  rw [deningerCollarExchange_apply, deningerPoissonSource_apply, deningerPoissonSource_apply,
    deningerMeyerCapFourier_coe, deningerPoissonLog_eq, deningerPoissonLog_eq]
  have hrefl := deningerPoissonValue_fourier_reflection h.2 (Real.exp_pos (-t))
  have hinv : (Real.exp (-t))⁻¹ = Real.exp t := by
    rw [Real.exp_neg, inv_inv]
  rw [hrefl, hinv, ← mul_assoc, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← Real.exp_add, neg_add_cancel,
    Real.exp_zero, Complex.ofReal_one, one_mul]

end

end RHTower

/-!
# Inversion in an affine space

In this file we define inversion in a sphere in an affine space. This map sends each point `x` to
the point `y` such that `y -ᵥ c = (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c)`, where `c` and `R` are the center
and the radius of the sphere.

In many applications, it is convenient to assume that the inversion swaps the center and the point
at infinity. In order to stay in the original affine space, we define the map so that it sends
center to itself.

Currently, we prove only a few basic lemmas needed to prove Ptolemy's inequality, see
`EuclideanGeometry.mul_dist_le_mul_dist_add_mul_dist`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

open Metric Function AffineMap Set AffineSubspace
open scoped Topology

variable {V P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [MetricSpace P]
  [NormedAddTorsor V P]

namespace EuclideanGeometry

variable {c x y : P} {R : ℝ}

/-- Inversion in a sphere in an affine space. This map sends each point `x` to the point `y` such
that `y -ᵥ c = (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c)`, where `c` and `R` are the center and the radius the
sphere. -/
def inversion (c : P) (R : ℝ) (x : P) : P :=
  (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c) +ᵥ c

theorem inversion_def :
    inversion = fun (c : P) (R : ℝ) (x : P) => (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c) +ᵥ c :=
  rfl

/-!
### Basic properties

In this section we prove that `EuclideanGeometry.inversion c R` is involutive and preserves the
sphere `Metric.sphere c R`. We also prove that the distance to the center of the image of `x` under
this inversion is given by `R ^ 2 / dist x c`.
-/

theorem inversion_eq_lineMap (c : P) (R : ℝ) (x : P) :
    inversion c R x = lineMap c x ((R / dist x c) ^ 2) :=
  rfl

theorem inversion_vsub_center (c : P) (R : ℝ) (x : P) :
    inversion c R x -ᵥ c = (R / dist x c) ^ 2 • (x -ᵥ c) :=
  vadd_vsub _ _

@[simp]
theorem inversion_self (c : P) (R : ℝ) : inversion c R c = c := by simp [inversion]

@[simp]
theorem inversion_zero_radius (c x : P) : inversion c 0 x = c := by simp [inversion]

theorem inversion_mul (c : P) (a R : ℝ) (x : P) :
    inversion c (a * R) x = homothety c (a ^ 2) (inversion c R x) := by
  simp only [inversion_eq_lineMap, ← homothety_eq_lineMap, ← homothety_mul_apply, mul_div_assoc,
    mul_pow]

@[simp]
theorem inversion_dist_center (c x : P) : inversion c (dist x c) x = x := by
  rcases eq_or_ne x c with (rfl | hne)
  · apply inversion_self
  · rw [inversion, div_self, one_pow, one_smul, vsub_vadd]
    rwa [dist_ne_zero]

@[simp]
theorem inversion_dist_center' (c x : P) : inversion c (dist c x) x = x := by
  rw [dist_comm, inversion_dist_center]

theorem inversion_of_mem_sphere (h : x ∈ Metric.sphere c R) : inversion c R x = x :=
  h.out ▸ inversion_dist_center c x

/-- Distance from the image of a point under inversion to the center. This formula accidentally
works for `x = c`. -/
theorem dist_inversion_center (c x : P) (R : ℝ) : dist (inversion c R x) c = R ^ 2 / dist x c := by
  rcases eq_or_ne x c with (rfl | hx)
  · simp
  have : dist x c ≠ 0 := dist_ne_zero.2 hx
  simp only [inversion]
  field_simp
  simp only [sq, dist_vadd_left, norm_smul, norm_div, norm_mul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul_abs_self,
    abs_dist, ← dist_eq_norm_vsub]
  field

/-- Distance from the center of an inversion to the image of a point under the inversion. This
formula accidentally works for `x = c`. -/
theorem dist_center_inversion (c x : P) (R : ℝ) : dist c (inversion c R x) = R ^ 2 / dist c x := by
  rw [dist_comm c, dist_comm c, dist_inversion_center]

@[simp]
theorem inversion_inversion (c : P) {R : ℝ} (hR : R ≠ 0) (x : P) :
    inversion c R (inversion c R x) = x := by
  rcases eq_or_ne x c with (rfl | hne)

/-!
# Exact finite diagonalization of the Möbius dilation family

Expanding a finite linear combination of the damped Möbius dilates at additive-circle
frequencies produces a divisor--Möbius incidence coefficient at every frequency.  Parseval then
diagonalizes the full quadratic form exactly.  This is the finite, unconditional algebraic core
of the all-scale identity `(G32b)` on the Route E research card.

The constant incidence vector is sent to the first pure tone by Möbius inversion.  Thus the
positive Gram geometry has no unaccounted boundary mode; any further point-evaluation estimate
must control the signed incidence coefficients themselves.
-/

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators Polynomial

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

private theorem sum_filter_identity_eq_dilation
    {α R : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [AddCommMonoid R]
    (s : Finset α) (w : α → R) {a : α} (ha : a ∈ s) :
    ∑ i ∈ s.filter (fun i => i = a), w i = w a := by
  have hfilter : s.filter (fun i => i = a) = {a} := by
    ext i
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_singleton]
    constructor
    · exact fun hi => hi.2
    · intro hi
      subst i
      exact ⟨ha, rfl⟩
  rw [hfilter]
  simp

/-- Divisor--Möbius incidence coefficient created by a dilation coefficient vector `c`.
At frequency `m`, the divisor `d` represents the Möbius frequency inside dilation `m / d`. -/
def mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient (c : ℕ → ℂ) (m : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ d ∈ m.divisors,
    c (m / d) * ((ArithmeticFunction.moebius d : ℤ) : ℂ)

/-- Möbius inversion sends the constant dilation vector to the unit frequency. -/
theorem mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient_one (m : ℕ) :
    mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient (fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) m =
      if m = 1 then 1 else 0 := by
  rw [mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient]
  simp only [one_mul]
  exact_mod_cast sum_moebius_divisors m

/-- Exponentially damped incidence coefficient at additive frequency `m`. -/
def dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient
    (x : ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℂ) (m : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient c m *
    Complex.exp (-((m : ℝ) * x : ℝ))

/-- Finite additive-circle polynomial carrying every Möbius dilation resonance through
frequency `M`. -/
def finiteMobiusDilationIncidencePolynomial
    (M : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℂ) : ℂ[X] :=
  finiteFrequencyPolynomial (Finset.Icc 1 M) id
    (dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient x c)

/-- Exact finite Parseval diagonalization of the full divisor--Möbius incidence form. -/
theorem circleAverage_finiteMobiusDilationIncidencePolynomial_norm_sq
    (M : ℕ) (x : ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℂ) :
    Real.circleAverage
        (fun z => ‖(finiteMobiusDilationIncidencePolynomial M x c).eval z‖ ^ (2 : ℕ))
        0 1 =
      ∑ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 M,
        ‖dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient x c m‖ ^ (2 : ℕ) := by
  classical
  rw [finiteMobiusDilationIncidencePolynomial]
  have hparse := circleAverage_finiteFrequencyPolynomial_norm_sq
    (Finset.Icc 1 M) id (dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient x c)
  rw [Finset.image_id] at hparse
  rw [hparse]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro m hm
  simp only [id_eq]
  rw [sum_filter_identity_eq_dilation (Finset.Icc 1 M)
    (dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient x c) hm]

/-- For the constant dilation vector, every finite frequency window containing `1` collapses
coefficientwise to the damped first pure tone. -/
theorem dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient_one
    (x : ℝ) (m : ℕ) :
    dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient x (fun _ => (1 : ℂ)) m =
      if m = 1 then Complex.exp (-x) else 0 := by
  rw [dampedMobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient,
    mobiusDilationIncidenceCoefficient_one]
  split_ifs with hm
  · subst m
    simp
  · simp

end

end RHTower

/-- The Möbius sum over all common divisors of two natural numbers. -/
def mobiusCommonDivisorKernel (a b : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  ∑ d ∈ (a.gcd b).divisors, μ d

/-- Möbius inversion turns the common-divisor kernel into the coprimality indicator. -/
theorem mobiusCommonDivisorKernel_eq_coprimeIndicator (a b : ℕ) :
    mobiusCommonDivisorKernel a b = if a.Coprime b then 1 else 0 := by
  unfold mobiusCommonDivisorKernel
  have h := congrArg (fun f : ArithmeticFunction ℤ => f (a.gcd b))
    ArithmeticFunction.moebius_mul_coe_zeta
  rw [ArithmeticFunction.coe_mul_zeta_apply] at h
  change (∑ d ∈ (a.gcd b).divisors, (μ d : ℤ)) =
    if a.gcd b = 1 then 1 else 0 at h
  rw [h]

/-- On positive coordinates, the kernel is exactly the `0`--`1` coprimality matrix entry. -/
theorem mobiusCommonDivisorKernel_succ_eq_coprimeIndicator (a b : ℕ) :
    mobiusCommonDivisorKernel (a + 1) (b + 1) =
      if (a + 1).Coprime (b + 1) then 1 else 0 :=
  mobiusCommonDivisorKernel_eq_coprimeIndicator _ _
